prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: original editorial hero illustration for a Spanish evidence-first science article about Shanidar A. Create ONE polished, landscape 16:9 raster illustration at high native resolution (approximately 1536 pixels wide or larger).
Primary request: a sophisticated, tactile, hand-painted editorial illustration of archaeological observation, rather than a reconstruction of an attack. A single recognisable human shoulder blade (scapula), rendered as an explicitly illustrative anatomical study, rests on an unmarked cream archival support on a quiet research desk. A simple magnifying lens lies beside it, signalling careful examination. The thin triangular scapular blade, spine and shallow socket should be plausible and coherent, without claiming to reproduce any particular fossil. Beautiful restrained chiaroscuro, subtle bone and paper textures, warm ivory against muted charcoal and earthy umber; commissioned museum/science-magazine visual quality, not flat vector clip art. The shoulder blade is the clear focal subject, readable at thumbnail size. Keep all important subject matter inside the central 70 percent so both wide hero and social-preview crops remain legible.
Evidence boundary: this is a conceptual illustration about examining a shoulder blade; it is NOT a photograph or a scientifically validated reconstruction of Shanidar A. Do not recreate a specific wound, fracture pattern, fossil specimen, measurement or anatomical trajectory. Do not show a spear or other weapon (none was recovered), an attacker, victims, blood, combat, care, burial, flowers, faces or a cave scene. Do not imply an intentional attack or identified assailant.
Constraints: generate from this text alone. No reference images, copied photographs, third-party artwork, logos, lettering, labels, numbers, scales, rulers, watermarks, borders, panels or dramatic sensational effects. No visible text anywhere. Non-graphic, calm and intellectually serious. The AI/conceptual caption will be supplied outside the image in the website.
